newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Avgold swells Q4 profit and eyes the world.
newsitem.headline: Avgold swells Q4 profit and eyes the world.

text.p: Newly-formed Avgold Ltd raised December quarter gold operations' profit 65 percent over the preceding quarter and said on Tuesday it would use its existing mines to launch an international future for the group.

"Through the restructuring we will use our old mines to build a future via the northern Free State into Africa and beyond," Jurie Geldenhuys, Avgold managing director, said at a presentation of the group's quarterly results.

Avgold is a member of the Anglovaal Ltd group and incorporates the activities of Loraine Gold Mines Ltd, Hartebeestfontein Gold Mining Co Ltd (Harties), the no longer listed Eastern Transvaal Consolidated Mines Ltd (ET Cons) and the Target gold project with effect from November 1, 1996.
Avgold was listed on December 31, 1996.
"We hope to create a modern gold mining company which will be favourably competitive with its international peers," Avgold chairman Rick Menell said.
He said Avgold was actively investigating interests in 13 African countries and that hopefully the group would have more to show on that front in the course of 1997.
Proforma results for the new gold group showed pre-tax and pre-capital spending earnings rise to 77.2 million rand ($16.9 million) in the fourth quarter from 46.8 million rand previously.
"We had very pleasing operating results this quarter," Menell said.

The average gold price received for the Avgold mines was significantly higher in the December quarter due to the rand's weakness against the dollar. It rose to 56,488 rand/kg from 54,201 rand/kg previously.

Avgold director of operations Tim Spindler said the Christmas holidays would adversely affect the current March quarter, despite the fact that attempts had been made to work in that potential lost time.

An 18 million rand windfall from uranium sales from Harties boosted December quarter earnings. Spindler said this had been a one-off big sale but that the potential remained for other sales, although perhaps not as large.
Cutting overall total working costs by eight million rand also helped to swell earnings, Avgold said.
But still a shadow hung over Loraine.
Although profit was up there, Spindler said a number of worrying features remained. Among these were falling ore grades and unions' demands for wages to be equalised with the rest of the industry.
"If we did that overnight we would put the mine out of business," he said.
Loraine had remained "very, very marginal."
The mine raised earnings to 3.69 million rand from 2.91 million rand previously.

Turning the spotlight onto ET Cons, Spindler said the division had moved back into profit after two lucky quarters and this looked set to continue. "I do expect this pattern to continue into the next quarter," he said.
ET Cons made a 3.82 million rand gold profit in the quarter compared to a 2.79 million rand loss previously.
A dump retreatment programme at the mine's Sheba division was progressing according to plan and the first gold from this operation was expected in June 1997.
A fire continued to burn at Harties No 6 shafts, forcing the closure of a high-grade area there. But Spindler said the shaft should be back in production by the beginning of February.
He estimated that 200 kg of gold had thus far been lost.
